A 6-year-old boy has a history of 5 bone fractures, 3 of them occurring after only minimal trauma.  His birth was unremarkable following a normal pregnancy.  The patient has been at the 50th percentile for both height and weight since birth, and he has reached all developmental milestones.  On physical examination, he is a pleasant, interactive child with small, malformed teeth.  Examination of the eyes is shown in the image below.

This patient's condition is most likely associated with impairment of which of the following processes?​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌
explanation:
This child has blue sclerae and a history of several fractures after only minimal trauma.  These findings are suggestive of osteogenesis imperfecta (OI), a predominantly autosomal dominant disease caused by impaired type I collagen synthesis.

Type I collagen, produced by osteoblasts, is the main type of collagen found in osteoid (ie, the organic portion of the bone matrix) and allows the bone to be somewhat flexible while still maintaining strength.  Type I collagen is also present in teeth, ligaments, skin, and sclerae.  Clinical manifestations of OI are caused by a deficiency of functional type I collagen and are variable, ranging from mild defects to fatal disease in utero.

Most commonly, patients have brittle bones that are prone to fracture and small, malformed teeth (dentinogenesis imperfecta), as in this case.  Patients may also have blue sclerae due to the deficient connective tissue allowing transparency of underlying choroid vasculature.  Some patients have short stature, whereas others have an average height.

(Choice A)  Osteopetrosis is an inherited condition that results in excessive bone mineralization due to a decrease in bone resorption by osteoclasts.  This can lead to dense, fragile bones and pathologic fractures.  However, this patient's blue sclerae and small, malformed teeth would not be expected.

(Choice B)  Endochondral ossification, the process responsible for long-bone growth, forms bone by replacing a cartilage template that is generated through orderly chondrocyte proliferation and hypertrophy.  This process is impaired in achondroplasia, an unlikely diagnosis in this patient of average stature.

(Choice D)  Long bones have multiple arteries that are essential for growth and maintenance.  Disrupted vascular supply to the subchondral bone within the epiphysis results in avascular necrosis.  Unlike this case, patients typically have pain and limited mobility rather than pathologic fractures.

Educational objective:In osteogenesis imperfecta, patients have brittle bones prone to fracture due to a decrease in functional type I collagen, a structural component of osteoblast-produced osteoid.  Other clinical findings of osteogenesis imperfecta can include blue sclerae and small, malformed teeth.​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌
